thread:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: Incident 3105055055 - High-rate auth failures observed against private-log-ingest. Suspicious traffic from 185.60.0.0/16. Potential leaked staging logs contain Authorization headers. Paging @sre-oncall @security_jamie @legal_ana

sre-oncall: ACK. I'm oncall, joining now. Gathering initial context.

maya: I see a spike in ingestion requests at 02:12 UTC from that CIDR, ~500 req/min. Pulling last-hour log batch.

indra: grabbing a sample. If logs include auth headers we need immediate rotations.

maya: sample snippet (masked):
```
[2026-03-17T02:12:45Z] INFO ingest: upload accepted user_id=123 auth='sk_live_********abcd' path=/staging/upload  src=185.60.10.23
```

sre-oncall: confirmed. That's a live-looking bearer token format. Blocking CIDR at the WAF and NG router now. Rule applied: WAF rule 8704, CloudEdge block (id: ce-block-3105).

ops-leo: Beginning key rotations for log-forwarder svcacct. Running: `./tools/rotate-keys.sh svc/log-forwarder && aws secretsmanager put-secret-value --secret-id /redwood/log-forwarder/creds --secret-string file://new-creds.json`

security_jamie: Good. I'll start invalidating any sessions/tokens tied to those keys and scan for similar exposures. Opening SEC ticket SEC-3105. Assume compromise until proven otherwise.

legal_ana: Adding legal for data exposure assessment. Any PII in those logs?

maya: Quick check: staging logs may contain user_ids and truncated emails in rare cases. No full payment info seen in this sample. Marking as potential regulated data — legal should triage.

sre-oncall: Also scheduling immediate S3 scrub of bucket `staging-logs-2026-03-17` for objects containing "Authorization:" pattern. Command I'm running: `aws s3 rm s3://staging-logs-2026-03-17/2026-03-17T02* --query 'Deleted'` (will snapshot first).

security_jamie: Running cluster-wide grep to find additional leaks: `grep -R "Authorization: Bearer" /mnt/logs/* | tee /tmp/auth-leak-scan.txt` -> got 8 additional hits across two staging clusters. We'll rotate all exposed tokens and rotate the service account keys used by forwarders.

ops-leo: Rotation in progress. Steps: 1) create new keypair, 2) deploy to log-forwarder instances, 3) invalidate old key in IAM, 4) confirm ingestion healthy. ETA ~22m. I'll post progress updates.

maya: Customer impact: preliminary — only internal staging project + two EU beta tenants received forwarded logs from staging bucket. No evidence of public endpoint exfil beyond the suspicious IPs.

sre-oncall: If any customer tokens are validated as leaked, escalate severity P2->P1. For now: mitigation underway, blockers: none.

security_jamie: Recommend also rotating KMS decrypt grants for the forwarder key and revoking recent short-lived tokens issued in last 24h where possible. I'll coordinate with ops.

legal_ana: I'll stand by for full inventory. If customer-identifiable data is confirmed, we'll draft notification templates.

pagerbot: Status update logged: mitigation in progress. Next auto update in 15m or on new action. Incident severity: P2 (Escalate to P1 if customers impacted).

ops-leo: Update: rotations pushed to 60% of forwarders, no ingestion errors observed. Continuing.

security_jamie: Update: SEC-3105 created, containment steps documented. Postmortem owner: @sre-oncall.

sre-oncall: I will own postmortem and runbook updates. After action items: add log-filter rule to redact Authorization headers at ingest and add retention exceptions for staging.

maya: Copy. I'll follow up with the scrub confirmation once deletes complete.

legal_ana: Noted. Will reach out if notification required.

pagerbot: Closing interim update. React with :white_check_mark: when you have local task ownership.
